text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parti Quebecois caves in to save Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard: Premier uses threats, theatrics, ultimatums to bend party policies his way.
- Ottawa to meet Canadian Airlines International, unions: No bailout plan, one source says.
- Hijacking began death flight: 52 survive crash near resort hotel.
- Stalking problem larger than expected: Prison may not deter, experts say.
- Politicians to decide fate of aid mission, Lt-Gen. Maurice Baril says. Systematic slaughter of Hutu men of fighting age feared.
- Big Six banks to top C$6-million: Fourth-quarter results will make 1996 profit a match for stellar stock market performance.
- Roll call in the boardroom: Attendence is under scrutiny, but some say it's a poor measure of a director's value.
- Guaranteed Investment Certificates earn more today, bank says: Royal Bank of Canada compares rates, inflation.
- Experts turning thumbs down for bonds, thumbs up for stocks.
- Canadian Airlines International CEO says wage-cut demand no bluff.

- 11th hour push for Canada Pension Plan deal: Ottawa is scrambling to get an agreement on CPP reform before Christmas but Ontario is hanging tough and employers need time to adjust 1997 payroll contributions.
